correctness.rationale: Explicit small edge-budget witnesses verified for m=0..11; classical Q(m) upper bound through m=9. For m=10/11 a triangle-bearing-core reduction forces any graph exceeding 7/8 ordinary triangles to include K5, by components, degree-two deletion, and complete mask enumeration of all 709801 relevant labeled graphs of order <=7. A direct argument proves any 3-coloring of K5 contains >=3 nonrainbow triangles, checked also over all 59049 assignments. An 11-edge graph with K5 has no extra triangle, so sharp upper bounds 7/8 follow. All quantifiers, boundaries, and exact calculations are documented and reproduced.

originality.rationale: The general 2026 inequality and earlier 2014 vertex-budget complete-graph results do not imply the exact m=10,11 optima: integer floors of the colorful inequality give 8 and 9, while five-vertex extremal results do not rule out a sparse graph on more than five vertices. The ordinary Kruskal--Katona upper bound gives 10 for each, and the sharp first colored deficit is a distinct statement. Related scientific statements and their logical implications were compared, not just titles. An unindexed equivalent theorem remains possible.
residual_risks: Unindexed or non-English literature might already contain this exact small-edge colored triangle profile.
The result is an exact finite boundary, not a uniform formula for all larger edge budgets.

value.rationale: The exact first loss from ordinary Kruskal--Katona realizability under the 3-color constraint is a natural finite-cutoff question, not an arbitrarily selected special graph. The edge-budget objective ranges over unbounded vertex count; the proof supplies a nontrivial finite-support reduction and sharp color obstruction. The plateau at m=10 and renewed increase at m=11 distinguish true discrete behavior from the real-valued colorful upper inequality. Does not claim all-budget theorem.
